# Online retail liquidation company to open location in St. Peters 

Developing News(First Alert 4)

By First Alert 4 Staff

Published: Jul. 29, 2026 at 5:45 PM CDT

ST. LOUIS, Mo. (First Alert 4) - MAC.BID, an online retail liquidation company, said Wednesday it would be opening a new location in St. Peters. 

The company said the new facility is expected to create more than 70 jobs and will open sometime this fall. 

The Pennsylvania-based company said the new facility will be located at 16060 Spencer Road. 

“We’re excited to become part of the St. Peters and the larger St. Louis Metro community as we open our 30th warehouse,” said Kellen Campbell, co-founder and president of MAC.BID, in a statement to First Alert 4. “We see real opportunity here, for the local economy, for the more than 70 people we’ll hire, and for shoppers across the St. Louis metro area looking for a smarter way to save.”

MAC.BID buys returned and overstocked items from retailers, then puts them up for auction starting at $1. The items then go to the highest bidder, with no reserve price.

# ID Logistics Plans 53,000 sqm Off-Grid Warehouse in the Netherlands

ID Logistics is building a 53,000 sqm off-grid warehouse at Tiel in the Netherlands, targeting BREEAM Excellent and up to 500 staff by October 2027.

ID Logistics is adding another oversized platform to its Benelux network. The French third-party logistics group has confirmed a roughly 53,000 sqm warehouse at Tiel in the Netherlands, sitting in the Rotterdam hinterland on the Medel business park. Delivery is set for October 2027, and once running the site is expected to employ up to 500 people across two shifts.

## Strengthening a dense regional network

The provider already operates 30 warehouses in the Benelux, some 750,000 sqm in total, having first set up there in 2013. Tiel extends that footprint closer to Europe’s main consumption basins and freight corridors. It connects to Rotterdam directly via the A15 motorway, which should help ID Logistics tighten inbound and distribution flows for its clients while adding resilience and flexibility to the wider network.

# DP World opens first multi-client 3PL warehouse in Saudi Arabia

Image Credits: WAM | Cropped by GBN

 Wed, 29 Jul, 2026 By Arya S Nair, Desk Reporter 

DP World has launched operations at its first multi-client third-party logistics (3PL) warehouse in Saudi Arabia, expanding integrated warehousing and distribution services to support the Kingdom’s growing consumer and industrial sectors.

Located at Riyadh’s Al Mashael Logistics Hub, the 15,250-square-meter facility offers more than 17,000 pallet positions, providing scalable storage, inventory management, and distribution services through a single integrated logistics provider.

The launch comes as Saudi Arabia accelerates investment in supply chain infrastructure under Vision 2030, driving demand for advanced logistics, warehousing, and distribution services across manufacturing, retail, e-commerce, and industrial sectors.

Operating as a non-bonded warehouse, the facility provides direct access to major transport corridors across Saudi Arabia and the wider Gulf region, enabling customs-cleared goods to move directly into the domestic market to reduce lead times

Edgistify adds a 68,000 sq ft Grade A warehouse at IndoSpace Luhari
ET Online Last Updated: Oct 16, 2026, 06:24:00 PM IST
Synopsis
Edgistify timed the launch for the festive season, the busiest time of the year for consumer brands
Luhari ships for websites, marketplaces, quick-commerce apps, and modern trade from one inventory pool.
Edgistify, which runs fulfilment for 70+ consumer brands, has added a 68,000 sq ft warehouse in IndoSpace's logistics park at Luhari, Haryana. It is the company's third high-grade facility in the Gurugram region, and new and existing customers are already shipping orders from it.
Edgistify timed the launch for the festive season, the busiest time of the year for consumer brands. Its two existing Gurugram sites are full, so Luhari gives brands one place to stock up early instead of spreading inventory across several partners when demand peaks. # GLS expands fulfilment offering with new centre in Denmark

GLS expands its fulfilment footprint with a new purpose-built centre in Kolding, marking the company's entry into fulfilment services in Denmark.

 07 October 2026 - 2 min 

- GLS Denmark has broken ground on a new fulfilment centre in Kolding, marking its entry into fulfilment services.
- The 5,000-square-metre facility is expected to be ready for use ahead of the 2027 peak season and can be scaled to 15,000 square metres to accommodate further growth.
- The investment supports GLS Group’s ambition to connect parcel delivery and fulfilment in a broader end-to-end offering for customers.

Amsterdam, 6 October 2026 – GLS is expanding its fulfilment capabilities with a new purpose-built centre in Kolding, Denmark. The new facility will mark GLS Denmark's entry into fulfilment services and support the Group's development of connected logistics solutions that combine parcel delivery with storage and order processing.
